_provenance.modeling_note: COUNT-0 PROSPECTIVE BRANCH written at the task's explicit instruction, at the same authoring standard as every other record in this packet, with every proxy clearly labeled. Full hand-authored damage model (5 hitboxes) adapted from the J-35 record's LO-fighter template (flying-wing UCAV sharing the internal-weapons-bay-plus-buried-engine layout logic), since no repo precedent exists for an unmanned flying-wing airframe. Internal weapons bays modeled as a pair sharing redundancy_group_id 'weapons_bays' (2-way redundancy, each bay independently loadable). Single dorsal buried engine (no twin-engine redundancy, since GJ-11-class UCAVs are single-engine per all public imagery). Folding wings and tailhook/launch-bar components included per the sourced Nov 2025 hook-down test and May 2026 launch-bar prototype. No sensor_ref/mounted_sensors wired (no public sensor-suite designation for the naval variant) and no ew_suite_ref (no public EW fit); default_loadout left empty and ammo.missile_count set to 0 reflecting the OOB doc's explicit 'kept at 0 in the default OOB' instruction, distinct from the weapons bays' non-zero capacity which represents the platform's designed potential rather than an asserted current loadout.

engine_ref.note: no naval-GJ-21-specific engine module was tasked (the task's engine list covers WS-21/WS-10/WZ-10/FWJ-6C/optional WS-19 only). Open-source analysis of the land-based GJ-11 widely assumes a WS-13-class single medium turbofan, but no such module exists in this packet or the wider repo. Rather than leave engine_ref dangling (unresolved _ref fields warn-and-continue at spawn rather than failing load, but the authoring_standard requires verifying resolution), this record reuses CSG_CN_WS-10H (written this packet for J-15T/J-15D) as the nearest-class proxy powerplant. This is flagged as an open issue in the final report: GJ-21's true engine class (WS-13, ~50kN thrust) is smaller than WS-10H (~130kN, twin-engine Flanker-class), so this proxy likely overstates GJ-21's thrust-to-weight and should be revisited if a WS-13 module is ever authored

rcs_profile_ref.note: reuses CSG_CN_J-35_RCS as the best available LO proxy, since a flying-wing UCAV like GJ-11/GJ-21 is understood to have comparable or better frontal RCS to J-35; no GJ-21-specific RCS profile was tasked separately
